items.title: El Nino could add to US inflation pressures in 2027, San Francisco Fed paper warns
items.summary: A San Francisco Fed study warns the current strong El Niño could drive US inflation up by 1 percentage point in 2027, despite temporarily boosting jobs. With inflation already above the 2% target, the climate shock adds further pressure on the Fed to raise interest rates.

items.title: Cement companies bet on price hikes to revive profitability in H2
items.summary: Cementmakers in India are experiencing a weak first half of the fiscal year due to rising costs. They expect price increases and seasonal construction activity to improve profitability. Price stability is noted after recent increases, which may help offset costs. Cement prices have risen and are expected to stay high in the coming months. The market leaders remain optimistic about further price improvements in the near future.

items.title: DOJ asks Supreme Court to block California counting disputed mail-in ballots
items.summary: The Department of Justice's request to the Supreme Court in the California case comes as it appeals dismissal of a lawsuit over Alaska's Senate election.

items.title: Irdai tightens ESOP norms, share transfer rules for insurers
items.summary: Irdai has implemented stricter rules regarding employee stock option plans for insurance companies to regulate ownership stakes. Senior executives and directors must seek approval to exceed prescribed shareholding limits under these plans. Insurers are required to monitor direct and indirect share allotments to prevent regulatory breaches.

items.title: Lumentum CEO touts 'enormous' opportunity in massive AI connectivity deal with Marvell
items.summary: The AI infrastructure deal is expected to close during the first half of 2028.

items.title: Zero-sugar drinks hit the sweet spot as sales double for PepsiCo and Coca-Cola in Sept qtr
items.summary: During the July-September 2026 quarter, consumer demand for zero-sugar and low-sugar beverages significantly increased across India. PepsiCo reported that sales of its low-sugar drinks doubled, while Coca-Cola also experienced similar gains. Higher sugar prices this year prompted many consumers to shift away from sugary drinks. Companies are prioritizing the production of low-sugar beverages to meet the rising market demand.

items.title: Govt consults seed, fertiliser firms on easing regulatory hurdles
items.summary: The Indian government is engaging with agricultural companies to address regulatory challenges that affect the sector. Consultations focus on updating the Seeds Act, 1966, to align with modern agricultural technology. Industry representatives have pointed out delays in approvals and licensing processes that hinder market access.

items.title: Aditya Birla Lifestyle bets on festive demand
items.summary: The company, which owns brands such as Louis Philippe, Van Heusen, Allen Solly and Peter England, reported flat like-for-like sales growth in September, against 5.3% for the second quarter of FY27. The slowdown comes just as the full impact of price increases begins to flow through in the December quarter, making consumer acceptance and discounting critical to sustaining growth.

items.title: This Is Such a Bad Time for a $115 Billion Tech Deal
items.summary: Timing is everything when you’re trying to pull off a mega-deal. And it’s hard to think of a worse moment for semiconductor designer Marvell Technology Inc. to unveil a takeover of laser specialist Lumentum Holdings Inc. at a $115 billion enterprise value.

items.title: Manufacturing activity eases in Oct as new order growth drops
items.summary: Manufacturing activity in India experienced a slowdown in October, decreasing from the previous month's growth. Despite this, the sector remained above its long-run average due to stronger international demand. A survey indicated that nearly 18% of manufacturers anticipated increased output over the next year, supported by fresh client inquiries.

items.title: 'Nobody will trust you...': SC junks Centre's plea against Vedanta arbitration awards
items.summary: The Supreme Court dismissed the Union government's appeal concerning disputes involving $99 million arbitral awards. Vedanta and Ravva Oil sought the enforcement of these awards related to the Ravva oilfield. The Delhi High Court had previously rejected the government's objections to enforcing the awards. The disputes originated from a 1994 production sharing contract between the petroleum ministry and various companies.

items.title: Judge tosses DOJ case against ex-FBI officials accused of lying about Hunter Biden probe
items.summary: Judge Zia Faruqui suggested the prosecution of ex-officials Nikki Floris and Bradley Benavides was rushed to come out ahead of the midterm election.

items.title: Budget 2027: Customs duty relief on 118 goods under review
items.summary: The Indian government is currently reviewing customs duty concessions applicable to 118 products set to expire. This review involves input from respective line ministries and industry stakeholders regarding these exemptions. Goods under review include materials for power projects and certain medical devices. A focus is on correcting the inverted duty structure to support local manufacturing initiatives. The outcomes of this review will influence the upcoming budget for 2027-28.

items.title: High Court restrains NPPA from action against AstraZeneca
items.summary: The Delhi High Court has issued a temporary restraining order against the NPPA's actions toward AstraZeneca Pharma. This order remains in effect until the next hearing date, January 11. AstraZeneca has argued that its product may not fall under controlled drug prices. The NPPA has accused AstraZeneca of overcharging for the inhaler from May 2016 to November 2025. AstraZeneca denies these allegations and claims compliance with the price regulations.

items.title: US manufacturing strengthens in October, input prices stay high
items.summary: US manufacturing activity accelerated in October, with the ISM manufacturing PMI rising to 55.5 from 54.5 in September, beating Reuters-polled economists' expectations. Strong consumer and AI-related business spending supported growth, but factory input prices remained elevated at 75.2, reinforcing concerns that US inflation could stay above the Federal Reserve's 2% target.

items.title: Making of Bullet Train: What India’s high-speed train will look like from inside; check out its high-tech interiors, passenger facilities & technology
items.summary: Union Railways Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw has shared a video offering a glimpse inside India's first Bharat-made Bullet Train, being manufactured at BEML's Bengaluru facility for the Mumbai-Ahmedabad corridor. The eight-car train will feature a test speed of 280 kmph, seating for around 557 passengers, accessible facilities, Wi-Fi-based infotainment and advanced safety and energy-efficient technologies.

items.title: VB-G RAM G grievance redressal rules set 15-day deadline
items.summary: The rules establish a multi-tier grievance redressal mechanism at the gram panchayat, block and district levels. Designated grievance redressal officers will be responsible for receiving, registering, inquiring into and disposing of complaints. Inquiries must be completed within seven working days.

items.title: Airlines seek govt support to protect Mumbai Airport slots
items.summary: Airlines at Mumbai airport are urging civil aviation ministry intervention regarding proposed capacity reductions planned for next April. Operator Mumbai International Airport Ltd intends to shift part of its international flight schedule to Navi Mumbai International Airport. While some airlines have consented to the changes, others seek more time to adapt to the new airport's infrastructure.

items.title: Railways adds 9,638 wagons to contracts worth Rs 3,925 crore
items.summary: Indian Railways is increasing its wagon procurement by 24.57% through additional orders from five suppliers. The incremental orders amount to approximately ₹3,925.41 crore and include 9,638 wagons. These wagons are intended for bulk commodities and will be supplied by June 2027. Suppliers involved in this contract include Titagarh Wagons, Jupiter Wagons, and Texmaco Rail & Engineering.

items.title: Clean energy investment helped India weather global energy crisis: PM Modi
items.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi stated that India's investments in clean energy have mitigated severe external shocks. He announced an ambitious target of adding 500 GW of new non-fossil energy capacity within the next decade. Modi emphasized the importance of energy security in relation to economic stability.

items.title: Meta eyes at least $20 billion from potential bond offerings, Bloomberg News reports
items.summary: Meta is reportedly looking to raise at least $20 billion through a cross-border bond offering to fund its expanding AI infrastructure. The potential debt sale follows its planned $97.5 billion equity fundraising, highlighting how major technology companies are increasingly tapping debt and equity markets to finance their artificial intelligence ambitions.

items.title: Institutional investors step up bets on private credit as insurers, pension funds and DFIs back new funds
items.summary: Institutional investors are now allocating more funds to private credit, significantly from insurance companies and pension funds. Neo Alternative Asset Managers has seen its second fund receive 22-25% contributions from these investors. Ascertis Credit's fourth fund also attracted commitments exceeding $700 million from multiple institutional investors. With increased interest in private credit, annual investment opportunities are now estimated around ₹1 lakh crore.

items.title: Anthropic revenue jumps 1,100% ahead of IPO as AI spending commitments near $900 billion
items.summary: Anthropic reported a 1,100% surge in third quarter revenue to $17 billion ahead of its planned IPO later this month. However, the AI company also disclosed a $23.3 billion net loss and nearly $895 billion in spending commitments, raising questions about AI infrastructure costs and investor appetite for its proposed listing.

items.title: A month after RBI’s rate hike, banks start raising deposit rates as liquidity shrinks, Bank of India the latest to move
items.summary: Domestic banks are beginning to increase their deposit rates due to shrinking liquidity conditions in the market. Bank of India recently announced a rate hike on deposits for various maturities, including a special 500-day option. This decision reflects the growing cost of deposits in the banking system as demand for credit rises. Banking system liquidity has significantly decreased from its peak in early September.

items.title: Govt set to tweak MSP norms for periodic price hikes of minor forest products
items.summary: The Centre is planning to restructure the minimum support price mechanism for minor forest produce. This change aims to provide periodic hikes to benefit tribal communities relying on forest produce. TERI has been tasked to study the current MSP framework and assess potential rationalization. Concerns regarding stagnant MSP rates sparking exploitation among forest-dependent communities have been raised in parliamentary discussions.

items.summary: India's central government anticipates a fiscal deficit exceeding budget estimates by Rs 1.2 lakh crore in 2026-27. This increase is primarily attributed to rising fertiliser, LPG, and petroleum subsidy expenses. Strong GST growth and disinvestment receipts may not offset the expected higher deficit. In addition, SBI Research recommends a revised long-term capital gains structure to generate additional revenue.

While Parachute volumes grew, revenue growth was limited primarily due to prior price reductions. Marico cautioned about ongoing inflation in crude-linked derivatives and vegetable oils impacting future margins.

The rules require complaint centres to operate 24 hours with human representatives available for assistance. Consumers will now have a shorter time frame of 15 days to appeal complaint resolutions.
